examples.ko: 그는 과거 발언이 뒤늦게 알려지면서 곤욕을 치렀다.
examples.en: He went through an ordeal when his past remarks belatedly came to light.

examples.ko: 어제 비행기가 8시간이나 지연돼서 곤욕을 치렀어요.
examples.en: My flight was delayed eight hours yesterday. What an ordeal.

production.promptEn: an ordeal, a rough time (___을 치르다)
production.contextHint: 곤혹 is the bewildered, cornered feeling

cloze.sentence: 공항에서 짐을 잃어버려 한바탕 {{}}을 치렀다.
cloze.en: I lost my luggage at the airport and went through quite an ordeal.

nearMiss.hint: 곤혹 is bewilderment (곤혹스럽다); what you 치르다 is an ordeal, 곤욕.

meanings: (fig.) one's head, as in a headache over a problem
(___를 앓다) to be at one's wits' end

collocations.en: to have a real headache over
to have one's head spin (from a problem)

examples.ko: 주차 문제 때문에 아파트 주민들이 몇 년째 골머리를 앓고 있다.
examples.en: Parking has been a headache for the apartment residents for years.

examples.ko: 애가 사춘기라 요즘 골머리가 아파요.
examples.en: My kid's hit puberty, so I've got a real headache these days.

production.promptEn: (fig.) one's head, as in a headache over a problem: ___를 앓다

cloze.sentence: 시는 늘어나는 관광객 쓰레기 때문에 {{}}를 앓고 있다.
cloze.en: The city is struggling with the growing amount of tourist litter.

examples.ko: 곰곰이 생각해 보니까 제가 좀 심했던 것 같아요.
examples.en: Thinking it over carefully, I think I went a bit too far.

examples.ko: 그는 편지를 몇 번이고 다시 읽으며 그 의미를 곰곰이 되짚었다.
examples.en: He reread the letter again and again, carefully going over what it meant.

production.promptEn: carefully, long and hard (thinking something over)

cloze.sentence: {{}} 생각해 보니 그 말이 맞는 것 같다.
cloze.en: Thinking it over carefully, I think he's right.
